findings.message: The new comment says the error message 'stays out of the prompt and the log, which keeps a reference only'. But the whole error object `e` is passed to `logError(`ai.tool ${call.name}`, e)`, and a logError helper normally records the error's message and stack. The new test's own example ('gross 285000 for kasun@lumenlabs.test') would then be written to the server log, so classified pay data and an email address end up in logs. No test checks what gets logged. Fix: log only the error kind or name plus the reference, or redact before logging. Then add an assertion that the logged output contains neither '285000' nor 'kasun@'.
findings.scenario: A tool throws Error('duplicate key: gross 285000 for kasun@lumenlabs.test'). The model gets only 'read_ticket failed (reference …)', but logError writes the raw message, with the pay value and email, to the server log.

findings.message: toolFailure writes the error-kind mapping twice. The FAILURES table maps names (ForbiddenError, ZodError) to phrases, and then an inline ternary maps codes ('forbidden', 'invalid_input') to the same phrases again. If one copy changes, the two can disagree. Fix: use one table keyed by name or code.

The new KeyTakenError skip path in syncSpecclaw has no test that is sure to reach it. The race test checks skipped entries only in `for (const s of sync.skipped)`, which passes without checking anything when no collision happens. The test also never requires at least one collision. If the sync wins every key, the KeyTakenError catch never runs, so a regression goes unnoticed. That includes defineService wrapping the error so `instanceof KeyTakenError` fails and the whole sync aborts. Fix: add a test that always collides. Create a proposal by hand that takes a specclaw key, run the sync through the real path, and assert that `skipped` contains that key and that the other records still sync.
findings.scenario: syncProposal's pipeline rethrows a wrapped error, so the instanceof check fails and the sync aborts on the first collision. The race test still passes on any run where the sync happens to get its keys first.

findings.message: The round-2 finding asked for a test showing 'distinct keys and nothing lost'. The fix instead accepts a lost record: when a hand-made create takes a key that a specclaw folder maps to, that folder is skipped. Nothing ever gets it back, so every later sync skips it again and the spec change never appears in delivery. The test writes this in as expected (`synced.length + sync.skipped.length === 6`). The cause is that hand-made and synced keys share one numbering. The collision is now reported, but the record is still lost. Fix: give synced and hand-made proposals keys that can't collide (a separate prefix or range, or a hand-made create that skips numbers specclaw has reserved), or reassign the hand-made key. Assert that all 6 specclaw records sync.
findings.scenario: RC has RC-001 synced. Four hand creates take RC-002 to RC-005. On this sync and every later one, specclaw 002-c1 to 005-c4 come back as 'key belongs to a proposal not created by the sync' and are never imported.

findings.message: The comment says the explicit project lock is 'Pinned by "a sync waits for the project lock"'. That test holds `FOR UPDATE` on the project row, and the comment itself admits the proposal insert's foreign key would wait on that lock anyway. So the test stays green with the explicit lock deleted, and it pins nothing about that line. Fix: correct the comment, or make the test observe something only the explicit lock causes, such as blocking before the `before` read.
findings.scenario: Delete the `select 1 … for update` line. 'a sync waits for the project lock' still passes, because the FK key-share lock blocks the insert.

findings.message: NotPendingError is thrown for anything that is no longer pending: already confirmed, already cancelled, or (since claim() returns null) an action id that doesn't exist or isn't the caller's. The page treats all of these as `handled` and moves the card to the 'done' state. It also tells the user to 'Check the record' when no record may exist. Fix: have claim() or NotPendingError carry the final state (confirmed or cancelled). Show 'done' only for confirmed and 'cancelled' for cancelled, and keep unknown ids as an error.
findings.scenario: The user cancels a pending 'Add proposal' card in tab A, then clicks 'Add it' on the stale card in tab B. That card turns to the done state with 'already handled, check the record', but nothing was written.

findings.message: The proposal retention clock now starts on `delivery.release.deployed`. That event's subject is a release, not a proposal row, and RetentionEntry has no way to say how an event maps to rows of `delivery.proposal`. The new defineModule check only confirms that the module emits the event, not that the event is about that table. The comment says the clock starts 'when a proposal's release reaches Prod', but nothing limits the event to Prod deployments, and the start isn't undone when the releasing deployment is voided. Fix: start on a proposal-level event (for example the phase change to released, which phaseEvent already emits per proposal), or add a declared subject or key mapping to `start`. Then check at load that the event's subject is the retained table.
findings.scenario: Release R with proposals P1 and P2 reaches Prod and emits delivery.release.deployed{id: R}. The retention engine matches the event to rows by subject id, finds no proposal with id R, and P1 and P2 only get the one-year idle fallback, not the documented 7 years from release.

findings.message: The svg aria-label recomputes 'last reached stage in own order' inline (sort by position, filter status, .at(-1)) instead of using mapRow's lastReached. That gives two copies of the same rule. Fix: build the label from mapRow(r, columns).stations.
